subject: Renewal conversation: commit toggle + rate buffer request
messages:
From: Sasha Nguyen <sasha@arborlabs.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arbor Labs Procurement <procurement@arborlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal / capacity bump — looking for short-term price stability

Hi Michael + Laura,

Hope you had a great weekend. Our team reviewed May usage and we expect a ~45% increase in token consumption over the next 6 months due to a new feature launch (embedding + RAG). We want to ensure continuity and keep unit economics predictable while we finalize internal budgeting.

Current commitment: 12M tokens / month (annual).
Requested posture: explore a near-term commit increase to 18M tokens / month and a temporary pricing stability commitment for 9–12 months while we validate the uplift.

Questions:
- Can Redwood offer a temporary rate buffer / price hold if we increase commit by ~50% for the next 12 months?
- Would a partial commit toggle be possible (start at +30% committed for 3 months, then step to +50% on signature)?
- Any credits for overages during the ramp window?

I've attached a short usage extract (arbor_usage_May2028.pdf) and a PO draft for internal review. Procurement will need an explicit renewal roadmap and a doc that ties the price hold to commit thresholds.

Thanks — Sasha
Sasha Nguyen
Head of Product
Arbor Labs

--
Attachment: arbor_usage_May2028.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Nguyen <sasha@arborlabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal / capacity bump — looking for short-term price stability

Sasha — thanks for the context and the usage extract. Quick first pass from our side below.

Summary proposal (framework):
- Temporary rate buffer: Redwood can hold the current unit rate for up to 12 months if Arbor signs an updated commit for at least +30% on month 1, with a staged step to +50% within 90 days.
- Credits: For the first 60 days after signature, any usage above the committed amount will be credited at 50% of the overage rate (applied as invoice credit the following month) to ease the ramp.
- True-up: Standard quarterly true-up cadence; no surprise termination fees if usage drops below new commit after month 6, but subject to a 30-day notice.
- Term: 12-month renewal term to start on the amended effective date.

I attached a draft terms sheet (MG-terms-v1.pdf) that lays this out with simple thresholds. Open items for your team: confirmation of step schedule (start +30% then +20% more at day 90), whether procurement requires an SLA amendment, and whether the price hold needs to be limited to specific model families (text-generation vs embedding compute).

If that direction works, Laura can convert to a formal proposal and we can circulate to legal for a quick addendum. If you prefer a shorter hold (9 months), we can tighten the credit window and preserve the staged commit.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: MG-terms-v1.pdf (Redwood draft: temporary rate buffer and staged commit toggles)

From: Sasha Nguyen <sasha@arborlabs.com>

Cc: Arbor Labs Procurement <procurement@arborlabs.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal / capacity bump — looking for short-term price stability

Hi Michael — appreciate the speedy reply and the clear framework. A few clarifications from procurement and product: 

1) Staged schedule: procurement is comfortable with +30% on signature but they want the second step to be optional (Arbor can elect to move to +50% within 90 days). We need both an optional step and a maximum step so budget forecasting is accurate.

2) Price hold duration: Can we cap at 9 months instead of 12? Our FP&A prefers shorter holds tied to rollout milestones. If you cap at 9 months, we'd accept a reduction in the overage credit window to 45 days.

3) Model scoping: We only need the price-hold to apply to text-generation families for now; embeddings will be under evaluation and will be billed as usage until we finalize.

Procurement note: Please include SOC2 report link and the updated invoice cadence for the amended commit. Also attaching a preliminary PO for reference.

Thanks — Sasha

Action items:
- Olga: can you review the MG-terms-v1 with the two changes (optional +50% step and 9-month maximum price-hold, 45-day overage credit window)?
- Laura: please prepare a formal quote / amendment and a DocuSign link; align invoice cadence with procurement's PO draft.
- Sasha / Procurement: once we have the revised terms, confirm the elect-or-not checkbox for the step-to-50% and the billing contact for PO processing.

I will also include the SOC2 link in the formal doc. Expect a revised PDF and DocuSign by EOD tomorrow pending legal's quick pass.
